clue.text: Meditating for all that time …

definitions.note: the clue word is a participle; the answer is the noun for the act of meditating, as in 'lost in thought'

parts.note: for all that means nevertheless, though

explanation.surface: Someone has been sitting in contemplation for a very long while, and the sentence trails off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next across clue in the surface only; each has its own definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being deep in contemplation is being in thought, the mental act of reflecting on something.

clue.text: Understand heartless guy following model

parts.note: to twig is informal for to understand

indicators.note: heartless means the middle of the word is removed, keeping its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Grasp that an unfeeling man is pursuing a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' just sets the shortened word after TWIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Twiggy was a famous British fashion model of the 1960s.

clue.text: Shop exit

definitions.meaning: a retail store or ... selling goods

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a shop selling a maker's goods and a means of getting out.

clue.text: This will attract fish during boat trip

definitions.text: This will attract fish during boat trip

parts.words: This will attract fish during boat trip
parts.note: the whole clue describes something an angler scatters into the water from a boat to lure fish to the spot

explanation.definitionFit: Groundbait is bait thrown into the water to draw fish to where an angler is fishing.

clue.text: Trade union leaders stick up for royal family

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their first letters
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: Union bosses stand up for a royal family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick up for' reads as the phrase meaning defend, but 'stick' is the piece of wordplay, 'up' is the reversal signal, and 'for' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the English royal dynasty from Henry VII to Elizabeth I.

clue.text: … how Medusa's snakes may be put on?

indicators.note: to snake is to wind and twist, so the letters of the name writhe into a new order

parts.note: the possessive here gives all seven letters, its S included

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about how the Gorgon's serpent hair might be donned like a wig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snakes' looks like Medusa's famous hair, but it is a verb telling you to twist the letters of MEDUSAS; the ellipsis joins the surface to the previous across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume a manner or a garment is to put it on, so assumed means put on.

clue.text: A parish priest puts up rates

parts.note: raises means puts up, as with prices

explanation.surface: A local cleric increases the charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rates' looks like a noun for charges, but it is a verb meaning assesses.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to estimate its value, which is what appraising means.

clue.text: Vision in audio place

indicators.note: in audio means as heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: sight is the faculty of vision

explanation.surface: A view in a recording of a location.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a place or location, as in a building site.

clue.text: He wrote about the past master having gold buried in earth

parts.note: MA is Master of Arts

indicators.note: buried in means one item is placed inside another

parts.note: clay is a kind of earth
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A historian is described as a master with gold hidden in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Babington Macaulay wrote The History of England; 'about' belongs to the definition, not a C for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Macaulay was a nineteenth-century historian, so he wrote about the past.

clue.text: Norfolk town always separate

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, a county in eastern England
ever means always

explanation.surface: An English country town is forever apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissever is an old verb meaning to cut apart, that is, to separate.

clue.text: Paint roller covers passage initially

indicators.note: the two words cover, or hold within them, the letters wanted

explanation.surface: A decorator's paint roller is passed over a corridor before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passage' reads as a hallway being painted, but it is a musical or written passage that comes at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: An introductory passage at the opening of a piece of music or writing is called an intro.

clue.text: Pickpockets — parasites and fools

parts.note: dip is slang for a pickpocket
ticks are blood-sucking parasites

explanation.surface: A list of three kinds of undesirable: thieves, bloodsuckers and idiots.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipstick is informal slang for a stupid person, so dipsticks are fools.

clue.text: Wisdom displayed by King George, say, as a golfer

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
EG, for example, is what 'say' means in 'a fruit, say'
Norman Wisdom was a British comic actor, so his first name stands in for his surname

explanation.surface: A royal's sagacity is shown off on the golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: Norman Wisdom was a much-loved British slapstick film comedian; 'displayed by' just sets NORMAN beside the royal and 'say' pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian Greg Norman was a world number one professional golfer.

clue.text: Electrical safety device for explosive lighter

definitions.meaning: a wire link in a circuit that melts when the current is too high
a cord or device that ignites a bomb or charge

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a circuit protector that melts under overload and the cord that sets off a charge.

clue.text: Spirit of revolutionary beasts? Extremely serious!

parts.note: something that has revolved has spun, so revolutionary suggests spun
kine is an old plural of cow, cattle or beasts

indicators.note: extremely takes the extremes, the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: The spirit of radical animals is described as very grave indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like political rebels, but it means having turned round, SPUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Spunkiness is courage and liveliness, which is spirit.

clue.text: This deflected battle spear

indicators.note: deflected means turned aside, so the letters of the two words are turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Armour describes itself as the thing that turned aside a spear in combat.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: 'This' points at the answer, and the anagram of BATTLE SPEAR makes the piece of armour that would deflect a spear.
explanation.definitionFit: A plate of armour worn over the chest is exactly what would turn a spear thrust aside in battle.

clue.text: Spoony, perhaps, with stirring demeanour

definitions.note: spoony is an old word for sentimentally in love; perhaps marks it as an example

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A lovestruck person is described as having an exciting manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirring' reads as exciting, but here it tells you to mix up DEMEANOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Being spoony means mushily in love, one kind of being smitten with someone.

clue.text: Reduce filler and stiffener

parts.note: down is the soft feathers used to fill pillows and quilts
size is a gluey substance used to stiffen paper or cloth

explanation.surface: Two materials, one for stuffing and one for stiffening, appear in an instruction to cut back.
explanation.definitionFit: To downsize is to make smaller, especially a workforce or home, so it means reduce.

clue.text: Haste makes waste

definitions.meaning: to waste is slang for to kill

explanation.surface: A twist on the proverb that hurry leads to loss.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for speed and a verb for killing someone off.

clue.text: Odd people in error in Eden

parts.note: originals are eccentric, unusual people
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some eccentrics make a mistake in the Garden of Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' appears twice: the first is part of the wordplay, the second belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian doctrine holds that Adam and Eve's disobedience in Eden was the first sin, inherited by all humanity.

clue.text: Cockney instrument for Trollope

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trollope' suggests Anthony Trollope, but it is the modern novelist Joanna Trollope.
explanation.definitionFit: Joanna rhymes with piano in Cockney slang, the dialect of East London, and is also novelist Trollope's first name.

clue.text: Insist upon a sure thing for the auditor

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the words are taken as they sound

parts.note: a cert is a certainty, a sure thing

explanation.surface: Someone demands a guaranteed result before a financial inspector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' looks like an accountant, but it means a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert is to state forcefully, which is to insist.

clue.text: Tots turn round

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the word for turn is read backwards

parts.note: a spin is a turn or rotation

explanation.surface: Small children spin about in a circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tots' looks like toddlers, but it means small measures of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A nip is a small drink of spirits, just as a tot is.

clue.text: Lawman going round capital to discover pests

indicators.note: going round means encircling, so one word is placed around another

parts.note: Moses received the Ten Commandments, the Law, so he is the lawman
Quito is the capital of Ecuador

explanation.surface: A sheriff tours a capital city to find out about its vermin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lawman' suggests a sheriff, but it is Moses, the giver of the Law.
explanation.definitionFit: Mosquitoes are biting insects regarded as pests.

clue.text: Queen meeting a sailor in the country

parts.note: Q is an abbreviation for queen, as in chess
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: The monarch meets a seaman out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the country' sounds like rural, but the country is a Gulf state.
explanation.definitionFit: Qatar is a country on a peninsula in the Persian Gulf.

clue.text: Concert for Maidenhead

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
read as Maiden head: the head, or first letter, of Maiden

explanation.surface: A concert is put on in the Thames-side town of Maidenhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Maidenhead is a town in Berkshire, England, but split as Maiden + head it gives that word's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A prom, short for promenade concert, is a concert such as those at the BBC Proms.

clue.text: Translate name found in prettier version

indicators.note: found in says one letter is placed within the other letters
a version is a rendering in another form, so the word's letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An instruction to translate a name that turns up in a more attractive edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' turns PRETTIER into ITERPRET and 'found in' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret is to render speech from one language into another, which is to translate.

clue.text: Wise random number generator

definitions.meaning: ... Wise was the straight man of the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise
the machine that picks winning UK Premium Bond numbers, Electronic Random Number Indicator Equipment

explanation.walkthrough: Premium Bonds are a UK government savings scheme whose prizes are drawn by a machine with this acronym.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one name: the comedian's first name and the acronym for the Premium Bond prize-draw machine.

clue.text: Former philosopher has daughter brought to light

parts.note: ex means former
David Hume was a Scottish philosopher
D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies

explanation.surface: A one-time thinker's daughter is revealed to the world.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhume is to dig up, and so bring to light something buried.

clue.text: Others must have a right to turn over a new leaf

parts.note: the rest are the others

explanation.surface: Other people must be entitled to make a fresh start in life.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning over a new leaf is beginning again, which is to restart.
